narrative:
The model determined that you have a 36% chance of being a bad credit risk. This probability was high enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

Your denial was driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. The length of the loan you requested had the strongest influence, and it worked in your favor because you asked for a much shorter term than most approved applicants. The second most important factor was the status of your checking account, which pushed the prediction toward denial. Having a negative balance puts you in a relatively small group—only 13% of approved applicants show a negative checking account, while most have either no account or a positive one. Your credit history was the third strongest factor and, like the loan length, it actually helped your case because you have a critical credit history that the model views as less risky than many other patterns.

Even though two of the top three factors spoke positively for you, the negative signal from your checking account status was strong enough, when combined with the overall profile, to tip the decision into the denial range.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account by clearing the negative balance and maintaining a positive one for several months. Once that picture looks healthier, reapply—the shorter loan term and your solid credit history are already working in your favor.
